what: Moving the mouse over the logo or a photo leaves a ripple-like trail behind it (OGL Flowmap — falloff .4 · dissipation .96), and the image is pushed 15% by that flow, within .2 around the mouse, red, green and blue are pushed separately (strength .05), and the faster the movement, the more rainbow light is mixed in at 10%. It rests 90 frames after the mouse stops
ease: Flow speed follows by .12 when moving and .02 when stopped · color-shift speed follows by .08 and shrinks by .985x every frame

options.dissipation: Flow trail (ratio kept per frame), default .96
options.fit: cover (default — fills the panel) · contain (whole image visible)

from.where: shared.js flow map logo (.t-logo) — the project logo placed on the table of contents ripples with the mouse

note: Images must be same-origin (or CORS-enabled) for WebGL to read them. With a transparent-background image, the transparent areas are left empty. The original feeds the shader’s mouse position flipped vertically relative to the flow map, and I kept that as is (color misalignment shows up at the vertically mirrored spot). Touch is not blocked (passive). Under reduced motion, only the image stays as is.
